page: Amazon Web Services i4i.large is a storage-optimized virtual machine running on the AWS Nitro System. It features an Intel Xeon 8375C processor built on the x86_64 architecture, providing 2 vCPUs across 1 physical core with multithreading enabled at a clock speed of 3.5 GHz. The CPU includes 54 MB of L3 cache alongside support for AVX-512 vector extensions and cryptographic instruction sets such as AES-NI and SHA-NI. System memory totals 16.0 GB of DDR4 operating at 3 GHz, and the instance includes a dedicated 468 GB NVMe SSD alongside a baseline network throughput of 1 Gbps. No GPU accelerators are present.

Benchmark evaluations reflect standard single-threaded execution paired with entry-level multi-core compute throughput. In single-core testing, the instance achieved a Geekbench score of 1558.0 and a stress-ng score of 1880.58, placing it in the mid-range tier. However, constrained by its two-thread, single-core profile, multi-core benchmarks scored in lower tiers, recording 1806.0 in Geekbench and 1923.48 in stress-ng. Memory subsystems delivered 14.18 GB/s read and 13.19 GB/s write in large block operations. Data serving metrics include 2.04 million Redis SET operations per second and 3.59 GB/s in static web serving throughput.

The primary architectural value of this configuration lies in low-latency local NVMe storage coupled with an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. This profile suits modest I/O-intensive workloads where direct high-speed local disk access is critical, yet intensive compute scaling is unnecessary. Typical applications include small-scale transactional databases, caching layers, write-ahead logging nodes, and read-heavy search indices where local storage capacity and caching headroom take precedence over parallel compute density.
description: Amazon Web Services i4i.large is a storage-optimized instance powered by a 3.5 GHz Intel Xeon 8375C processor running on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The configuration provides 2 vCPUs across 1 physical core, 16.0 GB of DDR4 memory, and a direct-attached 468 GB NVMe SSD, backed by 1 Gbps baseline network bandwidth without discrete GPUs. In synthetic evaluations, the platform demonstrates reliable single-threaded performance with a Geekbench score of 1558.0, though overall computational throughput is constrained by the two-thread limit, as seen in a multi-core score of 1806.0. Memory throughput reaches 14.18 GB/s for large uncached reads, while Redis caching throughput yields 2.04 million SET operations per second. With an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio and built-in solid-state storage, i4i.large is tailored for lightweight transactional databases, distributed cache replicas, log ingestion, and storage-heavy workloads requiring fast local scratch or persistent caching space.
